newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, rally seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, rally seen short-lived.

text.p: Chilean stocks surged at the close on year-end portfolio shuffling by institutional investors, but the market's fundamentals remain weak, said traders.
"I'm pessimistic. The bolsa could rise by another one percent but then stocks will start to fall again," said one dealer.
Other traders said the bourse, which has fallen seven percent in the last month, could find a new resistance level at 91 points.
The index ended up 1.19 percent at 88.72 points.
The general firmed 0.89 percent to 4,916.53 points.
Volume swelled to 10.3 billion pesos from almost four billion pesos in Tuesday's half-day pre-Christmas trading.

Traders said investors were concerned by a forecast from the Central Bank that consumer prices will rise 0.4 percent this month, which could make the government in danger of overshooting its inflation target of 6.5 percent.
Consumer prices have increased 6.2 percent in the first 11 months of the year.
Risers included power utility Emel which gained on news that U.S. electricity firm Pennsylvania Power & Light Resources will buy 25 percent of the firm for $106 million, said dealers.
Emel, Chile's third largest power distributor, climbed 7.95 percent to 9.5 pesos.
Other winners included power investment company Enersis, up 2.78 percent at 222 pesos and paper-maker CMPC which rose 2.17 percent at 4,700 pesos.
Losers included Banco O'Higgins, down 2.42 percent at 1,610 pesos and telecoms company Entel which lost 2.06 percent to 3,095 pesos.
